market_holds: Front-expiry straddle implies about 17.0% (ATM IV 287%, sealed 18:08 UTC), above the 14.7% median absolute reaction over the last seven prints (3 up, 4 down; +19.3% Aug-26, +12.3% May-26, -15.4% Feb-26, -14.7% Nov-25). The tape is a heavy de-rating: from 106.58 on 10-28 to about 77.2 intraday today (-28%), -7.0% today alone against IGV -0.6%, MDB -2.3%, SNOW -2.1%, DDOG flat and SPY -1.6% (Yahoo daily bars). The 50-day SMA is about $92 and the 200-day about $68 (MarketBeat, 11-17). Peers in the same complex fell as much or more: DDOG -40% from its late-October high with a print (beat and raise, -14 to -16% on a decelerating Q4 guide), DT -29% with a print (net new ARR flat, large deals slipped), MDB -24%, SNOW -19%. Consensus sits on the company's own guide: Q2 revenue about $486.7-486.9M against guide $486-487M, EPS $0.81 against guide $0.80-0.82 (Zacks/MarketBeat, 11-12 to 11-19), sales-led subscription guide $407.5-408.5M (+16.9%). Elastic has beaten every quarter (Q1: $478M vs $470M, EPS $0.70 vs $0.58) and calls its guide prudent and risk-adjusted. FY27 guide $1.998-2.010B (+15.2%), EPS $3.29-3.37. The sell side is split 17 Buy / 13 Hold. TD Cowen cut its target to $85 on 11-17, citing cautious industry checks, weaker third-party sales-rep reviews, observability risk and heavy insider selling, while still expecting a modest beat and a raise. Insiders sold about 4.59M shares (about $423M) in 90 days, including the CTO's 200k on 8-31. Put/call OI is 0.15, a call-heavy book.
view: This looks like a print where the price has already done much of the work in both directions. Elastic beats its guide almost mechanically, consensus sits at the guide, and a beat of 1.5-2% plus a raise passed through to the full year is the base case. What the stock trades on is the quality of that beat: sales-led subscription growth against the 16.9% guide, cRPO growth (21% last quarter), cloud consumption, and the size of the FY raise. The bear read-through from DDOG and DT is real but aimed at observability, which Elastic itself ranks as its slowest growth vector, behind security, AI and search. The bull read-through (hyperscalers accelerating, AWS +39%, Azure +48%, Google Cloud +103%; Elastic named a Gartner Leader in enterprise AI search on 10-07; the OpenAI partnership) is narrative the market already knows. Against that, this season has punished beat-and-raise software prints (DDOG, DT, TEAM -17%, NOW and FTNT) with only a few exceptions (Cloudflare +15.7%). The last same-quarter print (Nov 2025) was a beat and raise that fell 14.7% on soft net new cloud. With the stock already down 28% in three weeks and 7% on the day for no reason I could find, the bar is lower than it was. Whether a clean beat brings a relief move or a market in a rout sells it anyway, I cannot tell. I see no dated datapoint since the last call that the price does not already show.

recommendation.reason: Consensus equals the conservative guide, so a routine beat is expected and priced. The negative peer read-through (DDOG, DT observability) and the cautious channel checks are already in a 28% de-rating and a 7% pre-print drop. I found no dated evidence since the last call that points to a sales-led or cRPO surprise either way, so the direction is a coin flip on the quality of the beat and the market's mood at the open.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Sales-led subscription growth clearly above 18% with cRPO holding near 20% and an FY raise beyond the Q2 beat would argue for a relief rally from a washed-out level. Sales-led at or below the 16.9% guide, or a fall in cloud consumption like Nov 2025, would argue for another 15% drop.

self_critique: A long case exists: Elastic beats almost mechanically, and the stock comes in 28% off its high with a 7% unexplained pre-print drop and a call-heavy book. The last two prints rallied 12-19% from depressed sentiment, and Cloudflare showed a clean print can rip even this season. The short case is the season itself (DDOG, DT, TEAM, NOW and FTNT all sold on beats), the cautious channel checks, and last year's identical quarter falling 15% on cloud consumption. Neither side has dated, specific evidence the price lacks, so neither gets me to 65.
approach_notes: P4 (prove priced-in) and the peer-tape arithmetic helped. I could show the de-rating was sector-wide rather than assume it. P3's freshest-data rule found little here: Elastic gives no monthly data and executives were quiet since the call, so the search stopped at the peers.
